title: Create Better Presentations with SAP Analytics Cloud, Add-in for Microsoft PowerPoint
author: FredericBonta
text:
What This Course Is About 
 This course teaches you how to use the SAP Analytics Cloud, add-in for Microsoft PowerPoint . It connects your PowerPoint slides directly to your SAP Analytics Cloud stories. You can embed live charts, refresh data with one click, and deliver presentations that always show the latest information. 
 Who Should Take This Course 
 This course is designed for business users who create and deliver data-driven presentations. If you prepare executive reviews, board decks, or sales reports, this course is for you. You do not need any development skills. 
 What You Learn 
 The course is organized into five units. Here is a quick overview of each one. 
 Unit 1 – Getting Started You learn what SAP Analytics Cloud stories and widgets are. You also see how the add-in compares to other SAP tools for Microsoft Office, so you can choose the right one for each situation. 
 Unit 2 – Setting Up the Add-in You check the prerequisites, install the add-in from the Microsoft Marketplace, and connect it to your SAP Analytics Cloud tenant. 
 Unit 3 – Building Presentations with Widgets You add widgets from existing SAP Analytics Cloud stories to your slides. You then edit them directly in PowerPoint: apply filters, drill into data, and sort or rank values — without leaving your presentation. 
 Unit 4 – Keeping Presentations Current and AI-Enhanced You refresh widget data before a meeting so your slides always show current figures. You also use the AI-assisted summary feature to generate a text summary of any widget with a single click, then edit it directly on your slide if needed. 
 Unit 5 – Distributing and Governing Presentations You learn how to share presentations that stay connected to SAP Analytics Cloud data with others. 
 Three Benefits to Remember 
 Here are the three key advantages of using the add-in: 
 Always up-to-date data — One click refreshes all embedded widgets. You no longer need to rebuild slides every time your data changes. 
 Data exploration in PowerPoint — You can filter, drill, sort, and rank data directly on your slide, without going back to SAP Analytics Cloud. 
 AI-assisted summaries — The add-in generates a written summary of any chart in seconds. You review it and adjust the wording to fit your message. 
 This course gives you the skills to use it with confidence. Take the course, follow the step-by-step procedures, and share your experience with the community. We look forward to hearing from you. 
 Happy learning!

title: Feature in Focus: Five SAP Fieldglass Capabilities for Compliance and Scalability
author: SiobhnMcCullagh
text:
Welcome to the fourth instalment of our Feature in Focus series. In this edition, we showcase five SAP Fieldglass features that help organizations strengthen compliance and improve workforce scalability. 
 Each short video provides a practical walkthrough to help you unlock value from features you may not be using today. 

 Decision Form 
 A Decision Form is a configurable, guided request form that assists Buyers to capture and review information before creating the right procurement document, such as a Job Posting, Statement of Work (SOW), SOW Bid, Profile Worker, or Project, helping improve process consistency and reduce errors at the start of the engagement lifecycle. 

 Data Retention Policy 
 This feature helps organizations manage personal data by automatically identifying Worker, Job Seeker, and Resource records that are eligible for erasure, supporting compliance with privacy regulations and internal policies. 

 Rule Engine 
 This feature allows Administrators to configure and manage Approval Rules, conditional Activity Item rules, and Time Sheet rule associations, helping to enforce program policies, ensure process consistency, and support compliance requirements. 

 User Data Audit Log 
 The User Data Audit Log tracks field-level changes to individual User profiles via reporting. Each log entry includes activity date/time, the modification made, and the person responsible.​ 

 Find Similar People 
 The Find Similar People feature allows Buyers in SAP Fieldglass to quickly locate Workers and Users who share the same Job Code as a selected person. By surfacing known, qualified talent already in the system, it can help reduce time-to-fill and support workforce scalability. 

 Catch up on previous Feature in Focus topics and discover more SAP Fieldglass capabilities: 
 Feature in Focus: Reducing Cycle Times, Visibility and Analytics 
 Feature in Focus: Process Efficiency and Automation 
 Feature in Focus: User Experience 
 Stay tuned for the next topic in this series, coming soon!

title: Configuration to download Onboarding Documents Via Onboarding Dashboard
author: Nithiyasri_KM
text:
Introduction: 
 In SAP SF Onboarding, Candidates will upload documents if there is any personal data collection step has been configured. As a common business need, if the onboarding team wants to download and verify the documents, this post which mentions the configuration of the document download can be used. The below mentioned configuration has been tested in SF Onboarding 2.0 instance with 1H 2026 released update. 
 Requirement : 
 To download all attachments from Onboarding 2.0 dashboard for any user which has been attached in the custom MDF used for the personal data collection step. 
 Approach : 
 To facilitate this scenario following steps to be configured in the system as per the sequence, to begin with the steps we should have an access to create/edit the below MDF objects 
 Personal Data Collection (PDC) Custom Object 
 Attachment Field Configuration 
 ONB2DataCollectionUserConfig 
 Solution: 
 Step 1: Creating an Attachment Field Configuration 
 After creating and assigning a MDF Object in PDC step, The attachment field from the PDC Object need to be added in Manage data under “ Attachment Field Configuration ” one by one 
 While creating a new field configuration, Consider the below example: 
 The PDC object to be selected under the Object type. 
 Attachment field to be selected for which the field you are required to download the document for. 
 Assign the Attachment category as “ Custom New Hire ” since this is going to be a new hire in further steps and these documents will be stored based on the category. 
 Entity ID should be “ cust _subjectuser ” - Since this ID is used to find to which the attachments to be associated and we are linking attachments to specific Subjectuser. 
 Module - Onboarding to be chosen. 

 Step 2: Onb Data Collection User Configuration 
 After all the necessary fields created in the above step, the PDC object to be associated with the “ONB2DataCollectionUserConfig” since this object stores the attachments linked to each user’s internal ID. 

 Add the PDC objects in the association with below list: 
 Type : Join by column - since we are linking the Source and destination object. 

 Destination Object to be stored as “ cust_userConfig ” - whenever any attachment is added by the Onboardee that will be saved by this object against respective internal ID. 

 Source Object : As mentioned above, the attachment to be mapped with user’s Onboarding internal ID to fetch them in the dashboard, so use “ internalid” as Source Object. 

 Visibility - Need to be editable 

 Step 3: Final Result 
 After the above all configurations completion, we are set to start collecting the attachments from the Onboardee, which will be further visible to the Onboarding team to download and view from Onboarding dashboard under Onboarding Documents. 

 Conclusion: 
 While configuring the onboarding documents I have faced an issue where the documents were not visible in the dashboard and upon checking further I got to know that Step 2 which was mentioned above to be considered, Only when associating the PDC Object to ONB Data Collection User Configuration against Internal ID we will be able to download. 
 Hope This Blog will be useful and if you ran into any issues please drop a comment below. 
 Q&A 
 1. Only some attachment fields appear 
 Attachment Field configuration is missing for those fields 
 2. Document uploaded but not on the dashboard 
 Step 2 Association might missing or has wrong IDs configuration 
 3. Cannot able to view or edit the objects 
 Role permissions might be missing which was mentioned in the beginning

title: Handling Reversals and Cancellations in SAP Logistics Management
author: DavideFantini
text:
Reversals and Cancellations in Logistics Management 
 Logistics rarely runs in a straight line. A customer cancels an order hours after the picking team has already started. A carrier rejects a freight assignment at the last minute. A supplier delivers fewer items than expected. A data entry error slips through master data and propagates all the way into a warehouse task. These are not edge cases — they are part of daily operations in any distribution or manufacturing environment. 
 What makes the difference is whether your logistics system can handle them gracefully, or whether your team is left improvising. SAP Logistics Management (LGM) is built with exactly these situations in mind. It provides a structured, end-to-end set of rejection, cancellation, and reversal capabilities that let your team correct mistakes, halt unwanted shipments, and synchronize changes back to SAP S/4HANA — without leaving the system. 

 Outbound Process: Integration and the Sequential Reversal Model 
 SAP LGM is tightly integrated with SAP S/4HANA. Outbound deliveries created in S/4HANA are replicated to SAP LGM, where they become logistical demands — the central documents that drive transportation requests, warehouse requests, consignments, and pickup documents. 

 This integration means that every cancellation or reversal in SAP LGM has a corresponding impact in S/4HANA. The system enforces a sequential reversal model : you can only cancel or reject a process step if all downstream steps have already been reversed first. The further along the process a shipment has progressed, the more steps need to be unwound before the underlying demand can be cancelled. 
 The principle is straightforward — work backwards: 
 Reverse transport execution first (if active) 
 Then reverse warehouse execution 
 Then cancel transportation planning steps 
 Then cancel the logistical demand or delivery 

 Outbound Delivery: Declining, Cancelling, and Adjusting 
 For outbound processes, SAP LGM offers three distinct levers depending on how far processing has progressed. 

 Decline Outbound Delivery 
 When an integration task arrives with errors — due to master data issues or a customer cancellation shortly after distribution — the Monitor Integration Tasks app lets you decline the delivery at any time. No prerequisites apply. The system marks the task as Declined and creates a new task to communicate the decline back to the outbound delivery in SAP S/4HANA. 

 Cancel Logistical Demand 
 Once a logistical demand exists in the system, it can be cancelled from the Monitor Logistical Demands app, provided processing has not advanced beyond certain thresholds. Cancellation is always possible for demands with errors. For demands that are in progress, the consignment must not be in tendering, must not have been sent to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, warehouse activities must not have started, and carrier arrival must not have been confirmed. If any of those conditions are not met, the corresponding steps must be reversed first. 

 Reduce Outbound Item Quantities 
 When a customer reduces their order after the outbound delivery has already been distributed, you can reduce the item quantity directly on the outbound warehouse request in the Manage Outbound Warehouse Activities app. The updated quantity is automatically communicated back to the outbound delivery in S/4HANA. This is only possible before goods issue has been posted — after that point, a goods issue reversal is required first. 

 Once carrier assignment is underway, additional cancellation steps come into play. The behavior differs significantly depending on whether transportation planning runs through SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration or not. Understanding which scenario applies is the first decision point before taking any action. 

 Scenario A: Transportation Planning with SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration 
 When SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration is involved, a strict constraint applies: it is not possible to cancel a delivery (ODLV/LD) as long as there is an open communication channel — either an active tender or an open subcontracting confirmation. The carrier communication must be resolved first before the underlying demand can be cancelled. 
 When an outbound delivery / logistical demand is cancelled and there is no open communication to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration, the corresponding transportation documents (transportation requests, consignments) are automatically cancelled — provided that warehouse processing has not yet started. In addition, a cancellation is automatically sent to SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. 
 Freight tenders can be cancelled from the Manage Freight Tendering app from three statuses: Open, Awaiting Response, or Quote Received. If the tender is in Awaiting Response or Quote Received status, a cancellation notification is automatically sent to the carrier via SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration. 

 Scenario B: Transportation Planning without SAP Business Network Freight Collaboration 
 When an outbound delivery / logistical demand is cancelled, the corresponding transportation documents (transportation requests, consignments, freight orders) are automatically cancelled — provided that warehouse processing has not yet started. Notifications can be activated if the user wants to be informed about the cancellation of the outbound delivery. 
 In a Direct LTL scenario, you can also manually cancel the transport booking request in the Manage Consignments app after the request has been sent to the carrier. 

 Warehouse Execution: The Reversal Sequence 

 Outbound warehouse activities follow a strict reversal sequence. Each step must be undone in reverse order before the previous one becomes available. 
 Step 1 — Cancel a Picking Warehouse Task. If a picking task is still open (not yet confirmed), it can be cancelled from the Process Warehouse Tasks app. The task is removed from any work queue or bundle, and the stock reservation on the outbound warehouse request item is released. 

 Step 2 — Confirm Warehouse Task with Reduced or Zero Quantity. When a picker discovers that the available stock does not match the system quantity, the warehouse task can be confirmed with a reduced quantity — or even zero — directly from the Process Warehouse Tasks app on desktop or from the Mobile Warehouse Management app. The system then presents two options: 
 Reduce the quantity on the outbound delivery — used when the required stock is not available anywhere in the warehouse. The updated quantity is communicated back to the corresponding outbound delivery in SAP S/4HANA. 
 Create a new picking task from a different source bin — used when the required stock exists in another location in the warehouse. The system generates a new warehouse task for the remaining quantity from the alternative bin. 
 Step 3 — Release Stock from an Outbound Warehouse Request. If stock has already been picked but is not yet packed, the Manage Stock app allows you to release it from the outbound warehouse request. The picking status is updated, and the stock remains on the bin where it was picked — available for reuse without any further intervention. 
 Step 4 — Reopen Handling Units. Closed shipping handling units (HUs) can be reopened from the Packing Work Center, as long as staging is not yet completed. For parcel processes, reopening an HU automatically cancels the associated consignment, sends a cancellation message to the carrier, and invalidates the shipping label. A new label can be printed once the HU is repacked. 

 Step 5 — Reverse Staging. When items have been incorrectly packed or damaged during loading, staging can be reversed from the Manage Outbound Warehouse Activities app, provided goods issue has not been posted and loading has not been set to Completed in the pickup document. 

 Step 6 — Reverse Goods Issue. Once goods issue has been posted, it can be reversed from the Manage Outbound Warehouse Activities app. On success, the goods issue status returns to Not Started, the lifecycle status returns to Open, and stock with its handling units is recreated in SAP LGM. If the reversal fails in SAP S/4HANA, the lifecycle status remains Completed and requires manual investigation. 

 Transportation Execution: Correcting Physical Activities 

 The pickup document tracks real-time transportation milestones. All three key milestones can be reversed from the Manage Pickups and Deliveries app, and they must be reversed in order — departure first, then loading, then arrival. 
 Reverse Carrier Departure. This can be performed at any time with no prerequisites — making it the natural starting point when a departure was confirmed prematurely. 

 Reverse Loading Completion. Possible as long as the carrier has not departed. In an LTL scenario without transportation planning, consignments created after loading was completed are cancelled automatically, and new ones are created when loading completion is confirmed again. 

 Reverse Carrier Arrival. Possible as long as loading has not been completed and the carrier has not departed. 
 Together, these three actions ensure that physical activity milestones in the system always reflect what is actually happening on the loading dock. 

 Inbound Process: Cancellations and Corrections 

 SAP LGM provides comparable coverage for inbound processes, whether driven by purchase orders or inbound deliveries. 
 Cancel Inbound Logistical Demand with Errors. When an inbound delivery or purchase order is distributed to SAP LGM and the data check fails, the erroneous logistical demand can be cancelled at any time from the Monitor Logistical Demands app. Integration tasks are created to decline the corresponding inbound delivery in S/4HANA. Before cancelling, it is worth checking whether reloading the demand after fixing the underlying data is the better option — cancellation is irreversible and requires re-creating the document in S/4HANA. 

 When a supplier delivers fewer items than ordered, the inbound warehouse request quantity can be reduced directly in the Manage Inbound Warehouse Activities app. This supports partial goods receipt — the remaining open quantity stays on the purchase order for the next delivery. To fully reject an inbound delivery item , the quantity must be manually reduced to zero as part of the operational procedure. 

 Reverse Goods Receipt (GR). Available for both purchase order-based and inbound delivery-based processes from the Manage Inbound Warehouse Activities app. When triggered, SAP LGM sends a GR reversal request to S/4HANA. The inbound warehouse request shows a "Goods Receipt Reversal In Progress" status during processing. Once complete, the purchase order status is updated accordingly. All open (unconfirmed) putaway warehouse tasks must be cancelled before initiating the reversal. 

 What's Coming: Planned Capabilities 
 Relevant capabilities are currently on the SAP LGM roadmap: 
 Quantities after Putaway. Once all putaway warehouse tasks have been confirmed and stock has been stored in its final bin, standard goods receipt reversal is currently blocked. This planned capability is designed to allow quantity correction even after putaway is complete, communicating the corrected quantities back to SAP S/4HANA automatically. Until this capability is delivered, two workarounds are available: create a stock adjustment via the physical inventory procedure , or initiate a return delivery to vendor in SAP S/4HANA. 
 Warehouse Task Split. When a warehouse task is confirmed with a quantity less than originally planned, the system is planned to automatically retain the confirmed quantity on the original warehouse task and create a new warehouse task for the remaining open quantity. This ensures that outstanding stock movements are tracked and completed without requiring manual intervention to recreate missing tasks.

title: BTPEA Is Now Available in China: Bringing Consumption-Based Flexibility to SAP BAIP Customers
author: TiaXu
text:
SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA) was officially released in China on May 21, 2026 (SKU 8016044), bringing a consumption-based commercial model to SAP BAIP customers in the China market. 
 Why Is BTPEA in China an Important Milestone? 
 The launch of BTPEA in China marks an important step in expanding the commercial options available to SAP BAIP customers, creating opportunities to onboard more services into the local portfolio, and providing greater flexibility in how customers consume SAP BAIP services. 
 1. Introducing a Consumption-Based Commercial Model to China 
 Before BTPEA became available in China, Subscription was the only commercial model available to SAP BAIP customers in the China market. The introduction of BTPEA expands the available commercial choices beyond subscription-based commitments. 
 While Subscription is well suited to predictable workloads and predefined service requirements, BTPEA provides greater flexibility for customers whose consumption needs may change over time. Customers can use prepaid cloud credits across eligible services, switch between services as business requirements evolve, and pay for actual consumption within the terms of their BTPEA contract. 
 This flexibility is particularly valuable for customers exploring new use cases, managing fluctuating workloads, adopting services for which long-term consumption requirements are difficult to predict, or combining predictable subscription commitments with consumption-based cloud credits for more experimental workloads. 
 2. Enabling a Broader SAP BAIP Service Portfolio in China 
 Some SAP BAIP services are offered exclusively through the consumption-based commercial model. With BTPEA now available in China, more services can be considered for onboarding into the China market. For example, the following services are consumption-based only and are now available in China through BTPEA: Kyma runtime, SAP Build Work Zone advanced edition, Task Center, SAP Forms Service by Adobe, Object Store, Transport Management, Data Privacy Integration, etc. 
 This creates opportunities to expand the SAP BAIP service portfolio available to customers in China and helps make the China offering more complete and aligned with the evolving global portfolio. 
 Ultimately, a broader service portfolio gives customers more opportunities to access SAP BAIP capabilities and select the services that best meet their business needs. 
 What Is SAP BTPEA? 
 SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA) is a consumption-based commercial model that allows customers to consume eligible SAP BAIP services using prepaid cloud credits. 
 Under this model, customers make an upfront investment in cloud credits for the contract duration, with an annual commitment to consume SAP BAIP services. The cost of actual consumption is deducted from the available cloud credit balance. 
 BTPEA is particularly suitable for customers with established business plans who need flexibility to activate and deactivate services, switch between eligible services, and accommodate changing resource requirements without committing to a single service throughout the contract duration. 
 Key benefits include: 
 Flexibility: Switch between eligible SAP BAIP services as business requirements evolve. 
 Consumption transparency: Receive a monthly balance statement detailing service consumption and the corresponding costs. 
 Simplified commercial management: Use prepaid cloud credits across eligible services instead of managing separate subscription commitments for every service. 
 Volume-based discounts: Benefit from volume-based discounts, subject to the applicable commercial terms. 
 Access to an evolving service catalog: Access new SAP BAIP services as they become available under the consumption-based commercial model. 
 Customers are billed annually in advance. Any consumption exceeding the available cloud credit balance is billed in arrears at list price. Customers can purchase additional cloud credits at any time to help prevent overages. 
 BTPEA in China: Service Availability 
 Service availability varies by country, region, and contract terms. Customers can use the following resources to check which services are available in China and review the applicable pricing information. 
 1. SAP Discovery Center — Service Availability and Pricing Overview 
 Visit SAP Discovery Center 
 The SAP Discovery Center provides a non-legally binding reference for service availability and pricing. Customers can filter by Regions and Commercial Model to identify services available in China under BTPEA. 
 China currently has two available regions: 
 China (North 3) — cn20 
 China (Shanghai) — cn40 
 Note that not all services are available in both regions. 
 2. SAP BTPEA Price List — Contractual Reference 
 Visit the SAP BTPEA Price List 
 The SAP BTPEA Price List provides legally binding contract documentation. Customers can filter by Country and Contract Start Date to check service availability and pricing applicable to their contracts. 
 Please refer to the applicable contractual documentation for the final commercial terms. 

 Combining Subscription and Consumption-Based Models with a Hybrid Account 
 Many customers have existing SAP BAIP subscription contracts while also needing the flexibility of consumption-based services. A hybrid account supports both commercial models within the same SAP BAIP global account, allowing customers to combine predictable subscription commitments with consumption-based cloud credits. 
 This approach offers several benefits: 
 Reduced administration effort: Both subscription and BTPEA contracts can coexist under the same SAP BTP global account, so development and service consumption are managed in a single environment. 
 Commit more, save more — and pay only for what you use: Lock in attractive volume discounts through subscription commitments for predictable workloads, while using BTPEA cloud credits to cover peak periods or exploration projects where resource requirements are uncertain. 
 How Does Charging Work in a Hybrid Account? 
 The charging mechanism follows the applicable subscription entitlement quota and the consumption-based model. 
 When customers consume services covered by their subscription entitlement quota, that consumption is covered by the subscription model. Once consumption exceeds the subscription entitlement quota, the excess consumption is charged under the consumption-based model , using the available cloud credits. 
 This arrangement allows customers to retain their existing subscription commitments while using BTPEA to accommodate additional consumption. 

 China-Specific Considerations 
 While BTPEA is now available in China, there are a few operational considerations customers should be aware of. 
 1. Cockpit Cost and Usage Visibility 
 The Cost and Usage tabs in SAP BAIP Cockpit are available for the consumption-based offering in China, providing customers with visibility into their consumption and related costs. 
 Most of the planned Cockpit functionality is available. However, the Budget module is not yet fully available in the China offering. 
 Customers should take this limitation into account when planning their cost-monitoring processes. Further updates will be communicated as the remaining functionality becomes available. 
 2. Balance Statement Email Distribution 
 In the global process, balance statement (BS) emails are sent directly to customers. China follows a different process due to the role of CDC. 
 In China, CDC acts as SAP's third-party contracting partner — customers sign contracts with CDC rather than directly with SAP. As a result, all balance statement emails would be routed to CDC first, for centralized translation and forwarding to customers . 
 Key Resources You Should Know 
 The following resources are essential reading for getting started with BTPEA — covering the consumption-based commercial model, consumption monitoring, and balance statement verification. 
 SAP Help Portal: What Is the Consumption-Based Commercial Model? — Learn about the principles and benefits of the consumption-based commercial model. 
 SAP Help Portal: Monitoring Usage and Consumption Costs in Your Global Account — Understand how to monitor service usage and consumption costs. 
 SAP Learning: Verifying the Balance Statement — Learn how to review and verify balance statements. 
 SAP Document: FAQ Consumption-Based Commercial Model CPEA & Cloud Credits — Find answers to frequently asked questions about consumption-based commercial models and cloud credits.

title: The depreciation results differ between the two currencies - SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
author: evelynliu
text:
After running depreciation, upon comparing the Company Code currency and Global Currency, the exchange rate did not use the one defined by the customer. 
 The depreciation run does NOT translate the posting amounts for the individual currencies. In fact the currency translation takes place for the asset acquisition posting with the given posting parameters (posting date, etc.). 
 For example, an asset has the initial acquisition posting in period 11. The acquisition posting was done with 26,500.00 MYR 
 (= Company Code Currency). This posting amount was translated to 5,640.70 USD (= Group Currency). 
 Once the acquisition is posted, the system then calculates the depreciation amounts for each currency type (Currency Type = Company Code Currency or Group Currency). 
 The depreciation parameters for this asset in depreciation area 01 are currently: 
 Depreciation Key: LINK (= APC over Useful Life) 
 Useful Life: 10 Years and 0 Periods 
 Hence the system calculates the following depreciation amounts: 
 Company Code Currency (MYR) 
 Depreciation 2023 = 26,500 MYR x 10% [= 1/10] x 2 / 12 [2 periods pro rata for periods 11 & 12] 
 = 441.67 MYR 
 As the rounding setting is set to round the net book value, this calculated amount is adjusted to 442.00 MYR. 
 Group Currency (USD) 
 Depreciation 2023 = 5,640.70 USD x 10% [= 1/10] x 2 / 12 [2 periods pro rata for periods 11 & 12] 
 = 94.01 USD 
 As the rounding setting is set to round the net book value, this calculated amount is adjusted to 94.00 USD. 
 As shown above, the currency translation does not take place at the time of the depreciation posting. This is necessary so that the (original) APC is distributed evenly over the useful life. If the currency translation were to take place at every depreciation posting, it could not be ensured that the net book value reaches zero at the end of the useful life. 
 The amounts in different currencies can be viewed in the app "Manage Fixed Asset". In the valuation section for depreciation area 01, there is a dropdown list in the upper right corner of the value display control, in which the individual currency types can be selected.

title: AI-Assisted Role Wizard: Let your work speak for itself
author: chelsea_lueth
text:
Since introducing the Role-based Process Overview capability, people across organizations have been able to immediately see which processes are relevant to their work. Now, we're taking it one step further because finding the right role shouldn't require knowing your dictionary inside and out. 
 We're excited to announce an AI-driven enhancement to the Role-based Process Overview capability: an access aware intelligent setup wizard that finds relevant roles for you, based on how you describe your own work. 
 To enable AI-assisted Role-based Process Overview capability, your administrator needs to accept AI Terms and Conditions. 
 No dictionary expertise required 
 The original setup wizard asks you to select roles from your organization's dictionary. That works well when you already know what's in there but for new joiners, cross-functional contributors, or anyone switching teams, browsing an unfamiliar dictionary to find your roles can slow things down before you've even started. 
 With the AI-powered role wizard, you simply describe what you do and the wizard handles the matching. 
 How it works 
 Getting started is even easier now: 
 Find "My Process Overview" — Log in and locate the My Process Overview panel on the home page, just as before. 
 Start the Quick Setup — On your first visit, you'll see Role Wizard and can initiate it directly. Already have your profile set up? You can re-run it anytime to refine your roles or start fresh. 
 Describe your role and responsibilities — Instead of browsing the dictionary, type a short description of your job: your team, your tasks, what you own. The AI-driven wizard reads your input and surfaces the dictionary roles most relevant to you. 
 Review and confirm — The wizard presents its suggestions. You stay in control : accept, adjust, or add roles before confirming. 
 Enjoy your personalized view — Your My Process Overview generates automatically, showing the processes, activities, and RACI assignments tied to your confirmed roles. 

 Why it matters 
 The biggest friction point in the original setup was the expectation that users already know their organization's role taxonomy. That's a reasonable ask for a process owner but not for someone on day one, or someone who spans multiple functions. 
 By letting users describe their work in plain language and having AI close the gap to the dictionary, setup becomes accessible to everyone, regardless of how familiar they are with your organization's dictionary. 
 This means: 
 Faster time-to-value: New joiners can set up a meaningful process view in minutes, without a guided tour of the dictionary first 
 Better role matching: Describing responsibilities often surfaces relevant roles users wouldn't have found by browsing alone 
 The same personalized outcome: Everything that made Role-based Process Overview capability powerful such as access-aware content, RACI visibility, single-page clarity, remains exactly in place but now further accelerated by AI 
 Check out the demo video to learn about the details

title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Key Differences Across Products and Releases
author: AilaneKuhn
text:
Hi everyone, 
 This blog post continues our series on France Electronic Reporting. 
 In case you missed the previous blog posts: 
 See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available for an overview of the information that is available to help you navigate on the mandate. 
 See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Settings Checklist Based on Business Scenarios for a settings checklist based on business scenarios. 
 In this blog post, I would like to share some differences across products and releases that are worth pointing out. 

 Differences Across Products and Releases to Keep in Mind 
 In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition , SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition , SAP S/4HANA 2021 and higher , your entry point is the Run Statutory Reports app (App ID: F1515). For more information on statutory reports, see: 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Statutory Reporting 
 SAP S/4HANA: Statutory Reporting 
 Within the app, you select the report you want to run, and you can use the Manage Electronic Documents reporting activity that takes you to the Manage Electronic Documents app (App ID: F4306). You can use the Source for Invoice Reporting and Source for Payment Reporting processes to check the eDocuments that are created for a reporting period. You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date of electronic documents before they are included in a list. 
 Once you're ready, you can prepare the report run. Differently from lower releases, you check the statuses of the report submission within the Run Statutory Reports app, and once a report run is available, you can also show statutory reports from the Manage Electronic Documents app. Note that the document status and report run status might not get updated immediately. Once a response is received from the authorities, you can view the response file in the document status log. 
 After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority , you can generate a rectification by starting a new phase if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list , you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice. 
 Tip: 
 You can use the  Run Statutory Reports - France e-Reporting   app (ID: F1515_FR_4) to run the reports specific for France Electronic Reporting. For more information, see SAP Note   3721231 . 
 If you're new to using the Manage Electronic Documents app, you can find more information on the differences between the Fiori app and the Cockpit (available in lower releases) here: What are the differences between the Manage Electronic Documents app and eDocument Cockpit app? | SAP Help Portal .

 For more information on the procedure to generate each report, see: 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Generating the Customer Invoice List , Generating the Supplier Invoice List , Generating the Payment List . 
 SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2021 and higher: Generating the Customer Invoice List , Generating the Supplier Invoice List , and Generating the Payment List .

You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date or cancel electronic documents before they are included in a list. 
 Once you have the relevant eDocuments created for a reporting period, you run the Create Lists of Electronic Documents  report (transaction EDOC_FR_EREP) to generate the lists. You then go back to the eDocument Cockpit (transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) and you use the processes Invoice Reporting (FRINVREP_E) and Payment Reporting (FRPAYREP_E) to display the lists that have been generated, submit them to the authorities, and check the report submission statuses. 
 SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting , Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting , and Generating Payment Reporting . 
 SAP ERP: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting , Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting , and Generating Payment Reporting . 
 After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority, you can generate a rectification if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list, you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice. For more information on the rectification, see: 
 SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below : Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority . 
 SAP ERP : Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority. 

 We hope that this overview helps you find the information you need for the product you use and for your system release. Let us know if you have questions in the comments section below.

title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available
author: AilaneKuhn
text:
Hi everyone, 
 Many of you have already started working on the mandate for electronic invoicing and reporting reform for France, which introduces the mandatory digital invoice exchange and reporting of taxable transactions through an approved platform. 
 In this blog post, I would like to share an overview of the information that's available for you when using electronic reporting via an approved platform. 
 Legal Requirement and Scope 
 France’s compliance reform is based on two pillars: electronic invoicing and electronic reporting . The scope of electronic invoicing covers domestic B2B transactions, payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services. Electronic reporting , by contrast, covers domestic and international B2C transactions, international B2B transactions (including exports, intra-Community supplies, and other cross-border transactions), payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services. 
 The determining factor is establishment in France for VAT purposes, rather than merely holding a French VAT registration number . Companies established in France may therefore be subject to both pillars. Foreign companies that are registered for VAT in France but are not established in France for VAT purposes have no electronic invoicing obligation . However, they may be subject to electronic reporting for transactions carried out in France for which they are liable for VAT. 
 For more information on the legal requirement and the announcement of upcoming deliveries for France Electronic Invoicing and Reporting, see SAP Regulatory Change Manager . 

 More Information about New Features and Updates 
 Implementation Overview SAP Note 
 A starting point for checking the features that are made available is the Overview Implementation SAP Note. For the France mandate, there are two relevant overview SAP Notes: 
 For electronic invoicing: SAP Note 3413565 . 
 For electronic reporting: SAP Note 3713986 . 
 Although our focus in this blog post is on electronic reporting, there are some technical dependencies with the electronic invoicing solution. Therefore, always check the prerequisites stated in the SAP Notes before implementing anything.

 For information on the new features being released, you can look for the What's New topics:

 For more information on electronic reporting, see Getting Started with Electronic Reporting . In this topic, you find all the relevant settings required for the solution.

 For an overview of the electronic invoicing and electronic reporting via approved platform, see Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform .

 Tip : The links above take you to the latest version of the documentation of that product. Depending on the release of your system, make sure you select the specific release to display the relevant information for your system release: 

 WorkZone Group 
 The WorkZone group is available to help the community address questions, learn from other experiences, and used to announce daily updates in case there's a known issue, for example, if the government system is down. See France - SAP Document and Reporting Compliance . Stay tuned! 

 Troubleshooting and FAQ 
 As we learn from your experiences and business scenarios, we gather that information and include it in SAP Knowledge-Based Articles. For France Electronic Reporting, see 3756217 - eDocument France via Approved Platform Troubleshooting Guide . 
 If you haven't found information on the channels above, you can use the support channel and open a customer case to the following component: CA-GTF-CSC-EDO-FR-RE. 
 Please read through the information that is provided first, and you can also use the Feedback option on the Help Portal to help us understand whether the information is helpful. Please leave your comment so that we learn what didn't go well when you looked for specific information - That will guide us to the next improvements.

 We hope this gives you an overview of the different sources of information available to keep you informed on the latest updates for France. 
 Stay tuned for upcoming blog posts on electronic reporting. 
 Until next time,

 Issue Description 
 When I launch BAS, I am redirected to an identity-provider selection page with two options: Corporate IAS and Default Identity Provider. 
 Scenario 1: Corporate IAS 
 When I select the corporate IAS option and log in using my corporate account, authentication fails with the following error: 
 "Sorry, we could not authenticate you. Try again." 
 I am also unable to access the IAS Admin Console using my account. 
 Scenario 2: Default Identity Provider 
 When I select the Default Identity Provider, login proceeds, but I encounter two different errors: 

 Initially, SAP Build displays the following message: 
 "Access to SAP Build denied. To access SAP Build, you must migrate to use the SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication service." 

 Subsequently, BAS displays: 
 "Access Denied. You do not have the necessary roles to access SAP Business Application Studio." 
 The issue persists even in a Chrome Incognito window. 
 Troubleshooting Completed 

 Corporate IAS trust is active in the BTP subaccount. 

 OIDC is configured for the corporate IAS trust. 

 IAS is marked as available for user logon. 

 The BAS Developer role collection is assigned to my user. 

 Two user entries for my corporate email are visible in BTP: one under sap.default and another under the corporate IAS provider ( sap.custom ). 

 SAP Build Process Automation works normally in the same subaccount. 
 I have reviewed the following SAP Knowledge Base Articles: 

 KBA 3804871 – Error when switching from XSUAA to Identity Authentication Service (IAS) – Business Application Studio 

 KBA 3759388 – Access to SAP Build denied – Migrate to the Identity Authentication Service required 

 KBA 3770713 – Access to SAP Build Denied – IAS Migration Required for BAS / SAP Build 
 Questions 

 Can BAS display the IAS migration error even when corporate IAS trust is active and configured with OIDC? 

 Could having separate user entries under sap.default and sap.custom cause an identity-mapping or authorization issue? 

 What could cause corporate IAS authentication to fail with "Sorry, we could not authenticate you. Try again"? 

 Is there a specific migration or authorization check that should be performed for BAS in a TDD subaccount? 

 Has anyone encountered and resolved this combination of IAS authentication failure, SAP Build migration error, and BAS Access Denied?

title: SAP ECC to S/4HANA Migration: Which Technical Challenges Are Often Underestimated?

title: No-redirect modal login with PKCE on SAP Commerce Cloud 2211-jdk21
author: Darpit-Patel
text:
Hi all, 
 We are on SAP Commerce Cloud 2211-jdk21.20 with Composable Storefront (Angular). Since the JDK 21 OAuth rebuild, the password grant is gone and customer login uses Authorization Code with PKCE. 
 Our requirement is that login happens inside an ngbModal, with no browser redirect and no page reload. The standard flow and the custom login page option both send the browser through /authorizationserver/oauth/authorize, so neither fits. We also don't have a BFF or middleware layer. 
 The approach we are considering: 
 The SPA generates code_verifier and code_challenge (S256) and POSTs the credentials and code_challenge over HTTPS to a custom OCC endpoint. 
 The custom controller authenticates the user, creates a short-lived, single-use authorization code bound to the client, user and code_challenge, and returns it as JSON. 
 The SPA POSTs the code and code_verifier to the standard /authorizationserver/oauth/token endpoint, which verifies PKCE. 
 The SPA gets the tokens, closes the modal and updates its state with no reload. 
 Questions: 
 Is there a supported way on the new authorizationserver (Spring Authorization Server) to create and persist an authorization code from a custom controller, with the code_challenge attached? Which services or classes would you use? 
 Can the storefront be registered as a public client (no secret, authorization_code and refresh_token grants, requireProofKey=true) and complete this flow without the redirect round trip? 
 If not, has anyone achieved a no-redirect login UX on 2211-jdk21 another way, for example a small BFF running the PKCE flow server-side? 
 Are there security pitfalls with issuing codes outside the standard authorize endpoint? 
 We have looked at KBA 3757491 (PKCE on a custom login page) and the SAP Help page on the custom login page flow, but neither covers a no-redirect case. 
 Any experience or pointers would be appreciated. 
 Thanks!

title: SAP Brings Migration and Modernization Assistants to Customers’ Cloud ERP Transformations
author: Maura Hameroff
text:
To help customers accelerate their move to cloud ERP, SAP is bringing to life its migration and modernization assistants for transformation projects. 
 Accelerate your most complex, time-intensive transformation activities 

 Learn how 

 Supporting key workstreams, including data management, test management, custom code modernization, and business configuration, these assistants help organizations simplify transformation activities, accelerate project execution, improve decision-making, and increase readiness for cloud ERP adoption. 

 ERP transformation has become a business imperative for many organizations. Cloud modernization connects organizations to AI, automation, and analytics capabilities that legacy on-premises infrastructure could not support at scale. However, transformation programs can be complex, involving numerous stakeholders and requiring thousands of business and technical decisions. 

 This year at SAP Sapphire , SAP introduced new agent-led transformation tooling and outlined how migration and modernization assistants can reduce ERP migration efforts. 

 Today, four of these assistants are available to early adopter customers and are already supporting live cloud ERP transformation projects. 

 Migration and modernization assistants go live in customer transformation projects 

 ERP transformation projects require organizations to assess large volumes of business data, understand quality issues, evaluate migration implications, and prioritize remediation efforts across complex landscapes. The Data Management Assistant analyzes data quality metrics, identifies and prioritizes issues based on business impact, recommends remediation actions, and helps execute corrections through both automated and guided remediation approaches. 

 AkzoNobel, a global leader in paints and coatings, is currently on a RISE with SAP journey, consolidating its ERP landscape as part of a large-scale transformation. Participating in the SAP Early Adopter Care program, the company uses the Data Management Assistant to define data quality scope, evaluate issues across the landscape, and prioritize remediation efforts based on business impact. The assistant gives a structured, end-to-end approach to orchestrating workstreams and managing data quality throughout the company’s ongoing transformation. 

 “The Data Management Assistant gave us clear visibility into our most business-critical data quality issues and helped us prioritize remediation where it matters most,” said Thilak Selvam, Master Data Program Lead at AkzoNobel. “It reduced analysis effort, accelerated our planning, and provided a structured approach to maintaining data hygiene and quality controls as we prepare for future transformation initiatives.” 

 Defining test scope, preparing test cases, validating business processes, and ensuring representative data is available often requires substantial effort from both business and IT teams. The Test Management Assistant accelerates test preparation and improves testing effectiveness. By analyzing business processes, requirements, and user stories, it helps define test scope, identify critical business scenarios, generate test cases, and determine the test data needed to execute them. 

 Test cases are handed off to SAP Test Automation by Tricentis for automated execution, enabling continuous validation at scale. The result is less manual effort, improved coverage of business-critical processes, and greater confidence in deployment readiness. 

 The Custom Code Assistant helps organizations modernize their custom developments as part of the transition to SAP Cloud ERP Private and continues to support clean core compliance and cloud-ready transformation beyond initial migration. 

 It supports teams in assessing custom code, identifying migration and remediation opportunities, aligning extensions with clean core principles and SAP-recommended APIs, and adapting legacy applications for cloud-ready architectures. Acting autonomously, it classifies findings by complexity, applies available automated fixes, and generates AI-driven recommendations and code corrections for the remaining findings. The assistant helps customers determine where to adopt SAP standard processes and where custom extensions provide genuine business differentiation. This reduces technical debt, accelerates cloud adoption, and enables organizations to preserve the capabilities that set their business apart while taking full advantage of SAP innovation. 

 For customers adopting SAP Cloud ERP, the Business Configuration Assistant supports organizations in accelerating business design and implementation planning. It recommends and autonomously applies configurations tailored to the customer’s industry, segment, and business goals, supporting teams in defining scope, setting up organizational structures, and translating requirements into implementation-ready configurations. It also extracts source configurations, flags deviations from SAP target requirements, and maintains a full audit trail—reducing manual effort, improving consistency, and accelerating the path to a production-ready SAP Cloud ERP system. 

 Expanding across the full transformation life cycle 

 SAP plans to further expand the migration and modernization assistant portfolio across the transformation life cycle. Planned innovations include the System Analysis Assistant , which creates a customer-specific understanding of existing systems, configurations, and custom developments, providing the foundation for AI-supported guidance throughout the transformation journey and the basis for all other assistants, grounded in customer-specific system data. 

 In addition, the Project Management Assistant is planned to provide real-time project insights, proactively identify risks, and help orchestrate transformation activities across teams and stakeholders. 

 The portfolio will also be extended with the Rollout Assistant , which helps organizations align global templates with regional requirements, accelerating local rollouts while reducing effort for business and IT teams through AI-driven guidance. 

 Together with the Data Management, Test Management, Custom Code, and Business Configuration Assistants available today, these capabilities will offer customers a fully integrated, agent-led transformation experience that helps organizations simplify complexity, accelerate execution, and realize value from SAP Cloud ERP faster. 

 As SAP continues to expand its migration and modernization assistant portfolio, organizations will increasingly benefit from AI support across every phase of ERP transformation, from initial system assessment and project planning through implementation, go-live, and beyond. 

 Learn more at www.sap.com/MMA .

title: SAP and NTT to Cooperate on Delivering Trusted Sovereign Cloud and SAP Business AI Capabilities
author: SAP News
text:
TOKYO — SAP SE (NYSE: SAP) and NTT Inc. today announced their intention to cooperate in the areas of SAP Sovereign Cloud and SAP Business AI. 

 The planned collaboration aims to bring together SAP’s enterprise application portfolio, SAP Sovereign Cloud and SAP Business AI capabilities with NTT’s global infrastructure, full-stack integrated operations, deep industry AI expertise and global customer reach to help customers benefit from cloud and AI innovation while retaining control over sensitive data, operations, technology and security.  Supporting Sovereign Cloud Requirements 

 As an initial area of cooperation, SAP and NTT plan to work together to provide a broad set ofsovereign capabilities that combine the SAP Sovereign Cloud On-Site offering with NTT-managed infrastructure and operations to customers in key markets. 

 SAP Sovereign Cloud On-Site is SAP’s deployment offering for customers with stringent sovereignty, regulatory and compliance requirements. It enables SAP-managed cloud solutions to be operated in a customer-owned or customer-selected data center. This provides organizations with a high degree of sovereignty across local physical control, data residency and operational assurance, while helping customers address applicable local legal and regulatory requirements. 

 By combining the capabilities of SAP Sovereign Cloud with NTT’s global reach and expertise in advising, designing, delivering and operating secure infrastructure, the companies intend to support customers in geographies where strong local control is required. These capabilities are intended to help governments, defense organizations, defense industry companies, critical infrastructure operators and other regulated enterprises modernize mission-critical processes while maintaining control over sensitive data and operations and addressing compliance requirements. 

 Exploring the Value of AI 

 Building on this foundation, SAP and NTT intend to explore broader opportunities to help governments, critical infrastructure operators and highly regulated industries modernize mission-critical processes and adopt AI in a secure, responsible and sovereign manner. 

 “With this cooperation, SAP and NTT aim to give customers a practical path to cloud and AI innovation while maintaining the control, governance and trust they require,” said Dominik Asam, member of the Executive Board and Chief Financial Officer, SAP SE. “For public sector organizations and regulated industries, sovereignty is not just a compliance requirement, it is the foundation for resilience, competitiveness and the responsible adoption of AI. title: Aynı Yasal Duyuru, Aynı Değişim… Yoksa Değil mi?
author: hanyzanaty
text:
The Question 
 Open the roadmap. It looks familiar. 
 Open the H1 2027 Türkiye Payroll roadmap and the first impression is familiar. 
 Five Legal Changes. 
 New rules. 
 New dates. 
 New payroll work. 
 The normal question is obvious: 
 What do we need to change to stay compliant? 
 For TR00, the established payroll schema, that often means checking what is already supported, updating statutory parameters or enhancing existing logic where required, and keeping the solution aligned with applicable legislation. 
 Ama… 
 with TR01, our newer payroll schema, there is another question worth asking. Can we respond to the legal change without creating the next special case? 
 And sometimes there is an even more important question: Should we build something new at all? 
 That changes how I read this roadmap. Not as five identical development commitments, but as five opportunities to make a deliberate product decision. 
 ....... 
 TR01 is not about redesigning everything every time a new law arrives. 
 Compliance matters. Her zaman. But the best product response is not always a new payroll function or a new configuration table. 
 Sometimes we reuse something proven. Sometimes we automate manual administration. Sometimes a statutory scenario helps shape a reusable framework. And sometimes, after listening to the market, we decide that an implementation is not a priority for the current roadmap. 
 Some enhancements also began with our implementation partners, independently of any particular legal announcement. The legal changes give us a way to test whether those ideas can serve more than one scenario. 
 Here is how those decisions appear across the five roadmap topics, ordered by their current request delivery targets. 
 ....... 
 Five Legal Changes, Five Product Decisions 
 The laws differ. So do the solutions. 
 Nitelikli Hizmet Merkezi Gelir Vergisi ve Damga Vergisi İstisnası 
 First, Qualified Service Centers. 
 The legal change provides an Income Tax and Stamp Tax exemption on qualifying remuneration for eligible personnel, up to a statutory ceiling: three times the gross minimum wage for standard centers and five times for eligible special locations. The amount above the ceiling remains taxable. SGK contributions are not changed by this specific exemption. 
 For TR00 , we have not identified a relevant customer population. Consequently, a TR00 implementation is not planned in the current delivery scope . The legal obligation itself does not disappear for employers to whom it applies. 
 For TR01 , the more valuable direction is not another hard-coded exception for one type of employer. 
 Instead, we plan a Configurable Statutory Exemption Framework with two distinct approaches: one for exemptions applied to an eligible remuneration base, and another for exemptions on specific additional payments, allowances or benefits. 
 The design direction includes configurable wage-type eligibility, statutory percentages and ceilings, relevant employee or workplace conditions, and distinct SGK, Income Tax and Stamp Tax treatments. Existing net-to-gross processing should apply those results consistently rather than requiring a separate gross-up engine. 
 Qualified Service Center is the immediate legal scenario. The ambition is a framework that can support other statutory exemptions when their rules require it. 
 Yani… not every new exemption deserves its own permanent branch in payroll logic. 
 ....... 
 Kıdem Tazminatı Tavanı ve Vergiden Müstesna Çocuk Yardımı Tutarları 
 Next, child allowance. 
 For the second half of 2026, the Income Tax exemption thresholds for employer-paid child allowances are TRY 787.76 per child up to and including 72 months, and TRY 393.88 for children older than 72 months. Income Tax and SGK exemptions follow different statutory rules. 
 For TR00 , we can build on the existing child-allowance and SGK treatment. The planned work focuses on the age-band Income Tax exemption and on making the allowance easier to maintain: enter the amount per child and eligible child count, then let payroll calculate the total. 
 For TR01 , we can reduce a different manual step. 
 Instead of requiring HR to enter child counts repeatedly through age-band wage types, the planned enhancement reads IT0021 Family Members , determines eligible children and their age bands, and uses a configurable source for the employer-paid rate. 
 We are not introducing a separate SGK-to-Income-Tax-base configuration as part of this item. The objective is to automate the data that payroll already needs while preserving the established statutory calculations. 
 Less duplicate maintenance. More consistent eligibility data. 
 ....... 
 Uzaktan Çalışma Yönetmeliğinde Değişiklik Yapıldı 
 Then, remote work. 
 The September 2026 amendment strengthens contractual requirements for hybrid arrangements, including the distinction between on-site and remote working days and hours. Employers also need to report remote-working days correctly through the applicable e-declaration process. 
 Here, the lesson is that reuse can be better than reinnovation by invention . 
 For TR00 , reporting of remote-working days is already supported through the existing wage-type classification and e-declaration process, documented in SAP Note 3063529. The immediate task is to validate the customer configuration and the quantity passed to reporting, not to redesign SGK or Income Tax calculations. 
 For TR01 , the planned approach is to reuse that proven pattern: identify the relevant wage type through Evaluation Class 11, carry its remote-working-day quantity in payroll results, and report it using HTRCEDE0 . 
 We are not planning a new generic statutory day-count engine for this legal change. The source and treatment of partial remote-day quantities still need to follow confirmed legal rules and the appropriate existing configuration. 
 Sometimes the most scalable design decision is simply to avoid building something twice. 
 ....... 
 SGK Turizm Ücret Desteği Genelgesi Yayımlandı 
 Tourism Wage Support leads to a different decision. 
 This temporary measure covers the period from May to December 2026. It is an employer-side support ( destek ), not an employee SGK or Income Tax exemption. The statutory model uses eligible SGK premium days and a daily amount of TRY 116.67 , subject to the applicable employer-premium cap; SGK handles the official offset. 
 After considering partner feedback and identified customer demand, implementation of Tourism Wage Support is not planned for either TR00 or TR01 in the current scope . That is a product prioritization decision, not a change to employers' legal obligations. 
 Instead, we are prioritizing a separate TR01 enhancement that partners expect to deliver more everyday value: Recurring Meal Allowance . 
 Today, maintaining eligible meal days can involve repetitive entries and manual work when a daily rate changes during the month. 
 The planned TR01 enhancement uses a recurring IT0014 entry, derives eligible days from planned working days and applicable non-working-day information, and prorates the payment when the rate changes. It reuses existing SGK and Income Tax exemption processing rather than inventing new statutory meal rules. 
 One initiative is deliberately not being built now. Another, independent improvement is moving forward. 
 That is also a roadmap decision worth explaining. 
 ....... 
 2027 Asgari Ücret Tespit Komisyonu Kararı ve Gelir Vergisi Tarifesi 
 And finally, the annual cycle. 
 At the time of this draft, the official 2027 minimum-wage and Income Tax parameters have not yet been announced. Based on the usual cycle, SAP localization expects the relevant announcements toward the end of December 2026; actual values and effective dates remain subject to the authorities' publications. 
 For TR00 , the established priority is straightforward: update the relevant statutory parameters when confirmed, including the applicable severance ceiling on its own publication and effective-date schedule. 
 For TR01 , the annual update sits alongside a more substantial foundation initiative: bringing Severance/Indemnity calculations into the payroll schema . 
 The first planned phase covers core statutory severance and notice indemnity calculations, together with a separate monthly severance provision. For that provision, payroll evaluates accumulated service and the applicable full provision at month-end, then calculates the adjustment against the previous month's closing provision balance. 
 That provision is an accounting calculation, not an employee payment ; the precise financial and IFRS/TFRS treatment remains subject to validation. 
 More advanced termination settlement, off-cycle payment scenarios and annual leave provisioning or payout are possible future extensions, not part of the initial delivery commitment. 
 The opportunity is to establish a sound payroll foundation now without pretending that every related settlement scenario must be delivered at once. 
 ....... 
 Beyond Legal Changes — Improving the TR01 Foundation 
 But not every improvement needs a new law. 
 During our Türkiye Payroll partner roundtables, some of the most valuable feedback came from everyday implementation experience. 
 A deduction carried into the wrong payroll split after a company change. A configuration value that consultants must enter manually. An Excel export that removes leading zeros from statutory reporting fields. 
 Small details? 
 Perhaps. Until they affect payroll accuracy, require unnecessary workarounds, or interrupt statutory reporting. 
 That is why, alongside the five Legal Changes, we have also prioritized six TR01 corrections and usability improvements , targeting the end of November 2026. 
 They address three practical areas: 
 Payroll correctness: Improving carry-forward deduction handling, wage-type processing flexibility, and payroll schema execution. 
 Configuration usability: Making T7TR parameter maintenance easier through search help and IMG integration. 
 Reporting reliability: Preserving leading zeros in E-Declaration Excel exports to avoid invalid reporting files. 
 None of these requires a new statutory announcement. 
 They come directly from implementation partners working with TR01 and identifying where the solution can work better. 
 İşte bu. 
 Reinnovation is not only about introducing new capabilities. Sometimes it means fixing what gets in the way of using the capabilities we already have. 
 ....... 
 The Pattern 
 Put these decisions together and a different pattern emerges. 
 An established process → reuse and validate it before designing a replacement. 
 Repeated manual maintenance → derive information from existing employee or working-time data where appropriate. 
 A recurring statutory scenario → build a configurable framework when it creates genuine reuse. 
 Limited customer demand → make a transparent decision about what not to prioritize. 
 Everyday implementation friction → correct the foundation, even without a new law. 
 Three streams reinforce one another: statutory compliance, reusable product enhancements, and continuous improvement . 
 They do not always require the same technical response or the same delivery timeline. 
 ....... 
 The Design Principle 
 Each legal change invites a design decision — not necessarily new development. 
 TR01 is not simply TR00 rewritten. And it is not a redesign project hiding behind every legal change. 
 It is a habit of asking one extra question when change arrives: What is the simplest sustainable response — reuse, automation, configuration, a focused correction, or a conscious decision to defer? 
 Not every legal change will produce a reusable capability. Not every partner request will become a committed delivery. And not every proposed improvement needs a new engine. 
 But every decision should be clear about the customer problem it solves. 
 ....... 
 Haydi Konuşalım 
 The best product decisions begin with the right

title: Generative AI vs Agentic AI in SAP: Understanding the Difference
author: Myvizhipriya_Thangaraj_2810
text:
Overview: 
 When I started learning about Artificial Intelligence (AI), I kept thinking about one thing: How can AI actually help businesses in their day-to-day work, especially in systems like SAP? 
 We know SAP helps businesses manage different processes such as finance, procurement, sales, inventory and supply chain. But with AI becoming more common, I wanted to understand how it could make these processes easier, smarter and more efficient. 
 While exploring on this topic, I came across two termsinologies that caught my attention: Generative AI and Agentic AI. 
 To be honest, at first, I found them quite similar and I wasn’t sure what really made them different. So, I started exploring how each of them works and how they could be used in real SAP business scenarios. 
 In this blog, I’ll share what I’ve learned so far, explain the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI in simple terms and walk through a few practical examples from the SAP world. 
 Let’s understand it step by step! 

 What Is Generative AI? 
 Creates content: Generative AI uses our instructions to generate text, explanations, code, and other content. 
 Helps with SAP tasks : It can explain SAP processes, draft functional specifications, help us understand ABAP code, and prepare test scenarios. 
 Needs verification: AI can make mistakes, so we should check its answers against our SAP system and business requirements. 
 How Does Generative AI Work? 
 Learns patterns: The AI model learns patterns from large amounts of training data. 
 Responds to prompts: We provide an instruction, and the model generates a response based on its training and available context. 
 Improves through follow-up prompts: We can ask for simpler explanations, examples, or summaries, but the results still need to be checked. 

 Picture 1: Generative AI vs Agentic AI 

 What Is Agentic AI? 
 Works toward a goal: Agentic AI can plan and coordinate multiple steps to solve a problem. 
 Uses connected tools: In SAP, an AI agent could check invoice details, compare purchase orders and goods receipts, and identify discrepancies. 
 Supports next steps: It can recommend actions or perform approved tasks, depending on its integrations and permissions. 
 How Does Agentic AI Work? 
 Understand and plan: Identify the goal and decide which steps are needed. 
 Act and verify: Use authorized tools to gather information, check results, and perform additional checks if necessary. 
 Respond or take action: Present the findings, recommend a solution, or initiate an approved action. 
 In simple terms: Generative AI helps us create answers; Agentic AI helps us work toward outcomes. 

 Generative AI vs Agentic AI: What Is the Difference? 
 Let's compare both concepts using following SAP examples. 

 Picture 2: Which AI approach fits in the Task 
 They are connected concepts, and an AI agent may use a generative model as one of its core capabilities. 
 Generative AI focuses on generating useful outputs, while Agentic AI focuses on coordinating actions toward a goal. 

 How Does This Relate to SAP Joule? 
 1. Meet SAP Joule: Joule is SAP’s AI copilot that brings AI assistance into supported SAP applications and workflows. 
 2. Ask in simple language: Users can ask questions naturally instead of navigating complex screens for every task, depending on the available features. 
 3. Understand business context: Joule can help users find information and understand business processes using relevant enterprise context and authorized data. 
 4. Go beyond answers: Supported AI agent capabilities can coordinate multiple steps across business processes and applications, depending on integrations and permissions. 
 5. Know the difference: Generative AI creates content, AI agents work toward goals using tools and actions, and Joule provides AI capabilities within SAP’s enterprise ecosystem. 
 The key takeaway: In SAP, AI is not just about getting answers. It’s about making business processes easier to understand, support and execute. 

 What Should SAP Professionals Keep in Mind? 
 As AI becomes more relevant to enterprise applications, I believe SAP professionals should keep a few important points in mind. 

 Picture 3: Key AI Considerations 
 For SAP consultants, developers, and business analysts, these considerations are just as important as understanding the technology itself. 

 Generative AI vs Agentic AI: Pros & Cons 
 Like any technology, AI has its own pros and cons. In SAP, it can save time, reduce repetitive work, and make it easier to understand business processes. But it can also give incorrect answers, raise data security concerns, and require extra effort to integrate with existing systems. So, while AI can make our work easier, we still need to use it carefully and apply our own judgment . 

 Picture 4: Generative AI vs Agentic AI: Pros & Cons 

 Final Thoughts 
 I believe the first step is not to ask whether Generative AI or Agentic AI is better. Instead, we should ask what business problem we want to solve, what data and tools are required, and how AI can help us achieve the desired outcome safely and effectively. 
 AI in SAP is not just about generating answers. It is about finding practical ways to connect intelligence with business processes, reduce repetitive work, and help people make better decisions. 
 And understanding the difference between Generative AI and Agentic AI is a useful starting point for exploring that opportunity. 
 Thank you for taking the time to read this blog! If you found this helpful, i would love to hear your thoughts, feedback or questions in the comments. Let's keep learning and growing together! 
 I’m still new to blogging, so if you notice anything that could be improved or corrected, please don’t hesitate to let me know!!
